reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary:
The author is addressing a concern about the interaction between numa_balancing and shmem fix, specifically that the patch series does not handle the sashiko east-west false positive issue correctly.

The author addressed a concern about the patch series' behavior in mode 3 (placement + tiering), explaining that while the starvation counter isn't reset, everything still works as expected due to continued VMA scanning.
reviews.raw_body:
On 2026-11-10 10:04 -0500, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
... snip ...

Sashiko report feedback

---

Sashiko took issue with these skips, but its reported impact is
overstated.  It tries to point out a pre-existing condition:

  prev_scan_seq skips an update on a rare corner condition, but
  now the same skip applies to prev_placement_scan_seq.

In modes 1 (placement) and 2 (tiering), the behavior is exactly the
same as it was.

In mode 3 (placement + tiering) the result is that the starvation
counter isn't reset - but everything still works anyway because the
VMA is still being scanned.

I can follow up with *another* commit, but it's really low impact.
Not sure it's worth the churn.

-- 
~Gregory

2026-11-10.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue in NUMA balancing where VMA scan filters were preventing memory-tier promotion, leading to unexpected bandwidth utilization and poor performance on certain workloads. The problem was identified when testing fairness controls and found that numa balancing was broken due to recent shmem fixes. The patches plumb the scan reasoning into the prot_none injection while retaining placement-scan filtering, allowing for correct promotion of hot memory to local nodes. The series includes several related cleanups and is designed to be backported to stable kernels.

reviews.author: Bharata Rao
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that a patch in another patchset by Bharata Rao achieves the same effect as this one, and suggested that this patch is redundant.
reviews.raw_body:
I am carrying a patch in pghot patchset to base this shared folio check
on @vma, in the async migration case where VMA won't be available to check the
exec permission. The effect of that is to allow promotion of shared exec folios.

This patch achieves the same in more direct manner.

Reviewed-by: Bharata B Rao <bharata@amd.com>

Regards,
Bharata.
